messages:
alex_w: heads-up — ACME prod (ap-southeast) is seeing p99 token-gen jump from ~180ms to ~1.2s since ~08:12UTC. Customer trace shows an unexpected hop through eu-west before hitting the model. sample trace id: 4f12a3b2. logs + minimal trace below.

marie_k: :eyes: can you paste the trace span list and the request headers? also confirm this is hosted API and which model variant they hit.

alex_w: hosted API, model redwood/gpt-medium-v2. headers we captured: ``X-Client-ID: acme-frontend``, ``X-Requested-Region: ap-southeast-1``, ``X-Redwood-Region: ap-southeast-1``. but server-side span shows egress to eu-west-1. trace spans (chronological):
```
root -> edge-proxy-apac (edge-01) -> global-egress-router (apac-egr) -> transit-hop (eu-peering) -> model-serving-eu (eu-west-1) -> model
```

alex_w: traceroute from edge-proxy-apac to model-serving endpoint IP:
```
traceroute to 10.200.45.11 (10.200.45.11), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  edge-01.apac (10.1.1.2)  0.38 ms  0.34 ms  0.31 ms
 2  apac-egress-gw (10.1.2.1)  1.1 ms  1.0 ms  1.0 ms
 3  eu-transit-peer (192.0.2.45)  110.9 ms  111.2 ms  112.1 ms
 4  model-serving-eu (10.200.45.11)  113.0 ms  113.2 ms  113.1 ms
```

alex_w: tcpdump on edge shows outgoing nexthop to IP 192.0.2.45 even though model region preference is ap-southeast.

jun_lee: this looks like a routing decision mismatch at global-egress-router — probably fallback/route-selection judged apac capacity low and selected eu variant. can you check the route-decision log around the trace id? look for keys `fallback=true` or `preferred_region` mismatch. also check route-cache TTL and whether the client affinity cookie was present.

alex_w: grabbed route-decision log snippet: ``route_id=default user=acme pref_region=ap-southeast selected_region=eu-west reason=capacity_estimate:0.74 fallback=true cache_key=client:acme:route cache_ttl=0``

infra-bot: ALERT: routing-fallback-surge detected (2310006789) — 142 fallbacks from ap-southeast -> eu-west in last 10m. top cause: transient instance OOMs in apac-pool. See /alerts/2310006789

sara_ops: are these OOMs the recent model-worker oom-related autoscale events from last deploy? if so we might have a short window of degraded capacity and the router is aggressively falling back. we should temporarily raise fallback threshold or pin for the tenant.

marie_k: mitigation steps (short-term):
1) force region pin for ACME for 30m: add header `X-Redwood-Force-Region: ap-southeast-1` (customer-side) or set tenant override via console.
2) increase fallback threshold: `redwoodctl routing update --route default --fallback-threshold 0.15`
3) if urgent, disable cross-region fallback for ACME: `redwoodctl routes patch --id default --tenant acme --disable-fallback true`

marie_k: also start a targeted canary rollback of the model-worker change in apac pool (ops to confirm).

alex_w: applied tenant override via console for ACME (applied at 08:28UTC). pin header test: `curl -H "X-Redwood-Force-Region: ap-southeast-1" -H "X-Client-ID: acme-frontend" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` — initial p99 dropped to ~220ms on test runs.

jun_lee: follow-ups:
- collect more traces for 4f12a3b2-like ids to verify whether route-cache ttl=0 is a bug or expected on OOM events.
- check autoscaler logs for apac-pool (oom spikes, pod restarts).
- look for any recent change to global-egress routing policy (PR id or config rollout).

alex_w: will collect 100 sample traces and autoscaler logs, posting results here. for now ACME is stable with the pin. thanks team. :thumbsup:

sara_ops: monitoring dashboards + will pause any further rollout to apac until autoscaler root cause is fixed.

infra-bot: NOTE: incident ticket created #INC-2310, assigned to eng-infra.
